title: Potosi's silver industry depended on artificial lakes
body: In the 16th century, Potosi in what is now Bolivia was a major industrial centre. Aqueducts carried water from artificial lakes to hydraulic mills that processed silver ore from Cerro Rico.
takeaway: A valuable deposit is only one part of a mining economy. Processing it requires its own supply of power.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, City of Potosi (1987)
visual: an old stone mill and aqueduct below the slopes of Cerro Rico

title: Bhutan left the UN's least developed category in 2023
body: The UN created its least developed country category in 1971 to identify economies needing special support. Bhutan was among the original members and formally graduated on 13 December 2023.
takeaway: Graduation is a change in eligibility for certain international measures as well as a development milestone.
source: United Nations LDC Portal, Bhutan Graduation Status (2023)
visual: a small Bhutanese town spread along a Himalayan river valley

title: The Gini index measures distribution rather than total income
body: On the World Bank's scale, a Gini index of zero means everyone has the same income or consumption. At 100, one person has it all. Real estimates lie between those endpoints.
takeaway: Two economies can have the same average income and very different Gini values.
source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, Gini Index
